sections.overview: The Grey Plover is a long-distance migrant that breeds in Arctic regions and winters widely along coastlines.
sections.identification: It is the largest species in Pluvialis. Breeding adults have a black face and underside with a silver-spangled back; black axillaries are visible in flight in every plumage.
sections.habitat: It nests on Arctic tundra and, outside the breeding season, uses tidal mudflats, estuaries, beaches and salt marshes; it may also stop at inland waters during migration.
sections.diet: It probes or picks small invertebrates, including worms, molluscs, crustaceans and insects; prey varies between Arctic breeding grounds and coastal wintering sites.
sections.behavior: It makes trans-hemispheric migrations and is often gregarious on coastal feeding and roosting grounds outside the breeding season.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground in the Arctic; the clutch is usually four eggs.
sections.ecology: Unlike the European Golden Plover, P. apricaria, it has black rather than white axillaries. It is also a close relative of the Pacific Golden Plover, P. fulva, whose breeding and wintering range is centered farther east around the Pacific and Indian Oceans.
sections.conservation: BirdLife reports that the species was uplisted globally to Vulnerable in 2024 following widespread population declines.
